title: tenant-anchoring-and-ephemeral-edge-handovers-brainstorm
content:
Purpose:

This is a working brainstorm for an alternative to strict region-pinning: a tenant anchoring approach plus ephemeral edge handover flows. Goal is to reduce hard pinning operational cost while preserving auditable locality guarantees for regulated customers. This doc collects ideas, operator flows, telemetry signals, and customer comm templates that we can iterate into a formal playbook.

Scope:
- Target: Private + Dedicated customers with territorial requirements (GDPR, UK/EU, APAC data residency needs).
- Not in scope: hosted-only customers without contractual residency constraints.
- Focus on enforcement behaviour, evidence collection, and rollback/fallback mechanics.

Why a different approach? (notes to self)
- Hard region pins increase capacity fragmentation and waste at high churn.
- Many customers need locality for audit/evidence rather than absolute single-region processing all the time.
- Building flexible 'anchoring' allows small-window handovers to alternate regions during outages while providing audit trails.

Key concepts (rough definitions)
- Tenant anchor: canonical region(s) assigned to a tenant for primary data residency. Anchor is a policy object; not a strict runtime hard block.
- Soft-affinity window: time period where requests are preferentially routed to anchor region; requests outside window may be routed to secondary zones if needed.
- Ephemeral handover: operator-triggered or automated temporary reroute of a tenant's traffic to another region for N minutes/hours during incidents. Every handover must create an evidentiary bundle.
- Evidence bundle: timestamped manifest including TLS endpoints, ingress IPs, operator ID (or automation), KV-store snapshots (minimal), and routing traces to satisfy audit.

Operator flows (initial proposal)
1) Normal ops: requests route to anchor region. Telemetry tag: residency=anchor, route_reason=primary.
2) Graceful handover (planned maintenance): product schedule triggers handover window. Automation will: a) snapshot minimal tenant metadata, b) replicate allowed storage objects (per customer agreement), c) flip routing, d) produce evidence bundle, e) notify customer+sales.
3) Emergency fallback (unscheduled outage): SRE runbook triggers ephemeral handover if anchor region fails to meet SLO. Automation creates emergency evidence bundle and marks tenant state emergency_handover. On-call escalates to customer success if handover > 2 hours.
4) Rollback: rollback flow must validate data parity checks (hashes/manifest) before returning traffic to anchor.

Telemetry & traceability (must-haves)
- Per-request residency header: X-Redwood-Residency: {anchor_region, effective_region, route_reason, evidence_id}
- Evidence bundle ID that surfaces in logs, support tickets, and the console.
- Audit view: tenant -> chronological handovers with operator, automation run ids, and minimal payload hashes.
- Synthetic tests: weekly synthetic requests from zones to validate anchor adherence; fail if >1% mismatch outside scheduled windows.

Data movement constraints (privacy/compliance guardrails)
- Only minimal customer metadata and necessary tokens can be replicated to a secondary region during handover.
- By default do NOT replicate unencrypted KV blobs or customer files unless contract explicitly permits.
- KMS policy: keys that are region-bound will block handover unless escrow/dual-wrapping is provisioned. Add a new flag: anchor_allow_kms_escape = true/false per tenant.

Evidence bundle contents (minimal recommended schema)
- evidence_id (UUID)
- start_timestamp, end_timestamp
- trigger_type (planned|manual|auto|emergency)
- operator_id / automation_run_id
- anchor_region, effective_region
- list of ingress and egress IPs observed
- manifest of dataset hashes (if any replication occurred)
- links to routing traces (trace ids)
- policy_version at time of handover

Console UX notes (quick sketches)
- Tenant page: Residency tab -> show anchor, last handover, evidence_id link, and quick 'request justification' field for customers.
- Handovers timeline view with filters (planned vs emergency) + ability to download evidence bundle (ZIP).

Customer communication templates (short drafts)
- Planned maintenance: "We will perform a temporary traffic handover of tenant <X> from <A> to <B> on <date/time> to perform maintenance. All operations remain functionally identical; evidence bundle will be uploaded to <link>."
- Emergency notice (first touch): "Due to degraded capacity in region <A>, we have temporarily routed traffic to <B>. We are collecting audit evidence and will post a completed bundle after validation."

Risk matrix (high-level)
- Unauthorized replication of customer data: mitigated by default-minimal replication and KMS checks.
- SLA regressions during handover: measure and inform customers in contract.
- Legal pushback: require legal review for anchor_allow_kms_escape and explicit consent for data copies.

Open questions / TODOs
- What minimum manifest content is legally sufficient for auditors in EU/UK? (ask Legal: @Priya)
- How to handle customers who require absolute single-region processing (no copies ever)? -- likely must remain hard-anchored and exempt from handover automation, documented in contract.
- Edge cache TTLs: how long to keep cached artifacts in secondary regions? Need ops defaults and per-tenant overrides.
- Billing model during handovers: who pays for extra egress/storage? propose billing credit or tiered charges.

Action items (next steps)
- SRE: prototype evidence bundle format and a lightweight automation that can flip route for 10 test tenants (Diego) - due 2025-03-10
- Legal: draft checklist of minimally acceptable audit artifacts (Priya) - due 2025-02-28
- Product: wireframe residency tab + evidence download (Liam) - due 2025-03-05
- Dev: add X-Redwood-Residency header to frontdoor and trace propagation (Engineering: gateway team) - spike by 2025-03-03

Related artifacts / references (scratch links)
- Slack thread: #residency-ops (see messages from Feb 11-12 2025)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-REGIONAL-ANCHORS-142 (anchor policy draft)
- Jira: PD-9213 (handover automation epic)

Notes to self: keep language customer-facing: "anchor" sounds less technical and more contractual than "pin". We should prepare two vendor decks: one focused on technical ops and one on legal/compliance evidence.

Unresolved UX trade: letting customers self-enable emergency handovers via console may cause too many support tickets. For initial rollout, keep emergency handovers operator-only and allow self-serve for planned maintenance windows.

End of draft.
